name: Author and create a CRD
objective: CKAD › Application Environment, Configuration and Security. Drill EVERY CRD corner harder than the exam: author a typed CRD, create and inspect CRs, discover an installed CRD, list via plural/short name, enforce schema validation (required + enum), cluster-scoped CRDs, and a no-hint diagnose-and-fix on a CRD that won't serve. Graded exactly, per requirement.

questions.title: Author a typed CustomResourceDefinition
questions.teach:
A **CustomResourceDefinition** teaches the API server a new kind. In `apiextensions.k8s.io/v1` you set `spec.group`, `spec.names` (kind/plural/singular), `spec.scope`, and a `versions[]` entry with `served`/`storage` and an `openAPIV3Schema` typing the fields.

**Gotcha:** `metadata.name` MUST be exactly `<plural>.<group>` (`widgets.stable.example.com`) — any other name is rejected.
questions.prompt:
Create a CRD for a namespaced kind `Widget` in group `stable.example.com` (plural `widgets`, singular `widget`), version `v1` (served and storage), whose schema types `spec.size` (integer) and `spec.color` (string).

Target: `kubectl get crd widgets.stable.example.com` exists, scope Namespaced, and its `Established` condition is `True`.
questions.hint: Apply an `apiextensions.k8s.io/v1` CustomResourceDefinition. `metadata.name` = `<plural>.<group>` = `widgets.stable.example.com`. Under `spec.versions[0].schema.openAPIV3Schema` set `type: object` with `properties.spec` an object having `size` (integer) and `color` (string).
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: widgets.stable.example.com
spec:
  group: stable.example.com
  scope: Namespaced
  names:
    kind: Widget
    plural: widgets
    singular: widget
    shortNames: [wg]
  versions:
  - name: v1
    served: true
    storage: true
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          spec:
            type: object
            properties:
              size: { type: integer }
              color: { type: string }
YAML
kubectl get crd widgets.stable.example.com -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions[?(@.type=="Established")].status}'

verification.description: CRD widgets.stable.example.com: Namespaced, spec.size:integer + spec.color:string, Established

questions.eli5:
Imagine Kubernetes is a huge warehouse with a clipboard listing every **kind** of thing it knows how to store: Pods, Services, Deployments. If you walk up and say "store me a **Widget**," the clerk shrugs — "Widget" isn't on the clipboard, so it refuses.

A **CustomResourceDefinition (CRD)** is you teaching the clerk a brand-new kind by handing over a little instruction card. The card says:

- what **group** the kind belongs to (a family surname, like `stable.example.com`),
- the kind's **names** — its proper name (`Widget`), its everyday plural (`widgets`), and nicknames (`wg`),
- whether each Widget lives **inside a room** (namespaced) or out in the open warehouse (cluster-wide),
- a **version** that's turned on (`served`) and the one used for the filing cabinet (`storage`),
- a **shape** (schema) describing what fields a Widget has: a `size` that must be a number, a `color` that must be text.

Once the clerk reads and accepts the card, "Widget" appears on the clipboard and everyone can create Widgets.

**Watch out:**

- The card's **title must be exactly `<plural>.<group>`** — `widgets.stable.example.com`. Any other title and the clerk rejects the whole card.
- You must wait until the clerk says **`Established: True`** — only then is the kind really usable.
- Each version needs one `storage: true`; exactly one version is the filing cabinet.
- `served: true` is what actually turns the kind **on** — a card with nothing served teaches a kind nobody can use.
- The schema fields go under `properties`, with `type: object` at the top — forget the top-level `type` and the card is invalid.
questions.deepDive:
## Authoring a CustomResourceDefinition — full rundown

### Mental model
A **CRD** is a *schema registration*: it teaches the kube-apiserver a brand-new `kind` so that custom resources (CRs) of that kind can be created, stored in etcd, and served over REST exactly like native objects. The CRD is the *class definition*; the CRs you create later are the *instances*.

- The CRD itself is a cluster-scoped object of kind `CustomResourceDefinition` in group `apiextensions.k8s.io/v1`.
- The **kind it teaches** (e.g. `Widget`) lives in *your* group (`stable.example.com`).

### The exact manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: widgets.stable.example.com      # MUST equal <plural>.<group>
spec:
  group: stable.example.com
  scope: Namespaced                      # or Cluster
  names:
    kind: Widget                         # PascalCase, used in CR's `kind`
    plural: widgets                      # URL path + `kubectl get widgets`
    singular: widget
    shortNames: [wg]                     # optional nicknames
  versions:
  - name: v1
    served: true                         # expose this version over REST
    storage: true                        # exactly ONE version stores to etcd
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        type: object                     # REQUIRED top-level type
        properties:
          spec:
            type: object
            properties:
              size:  { type: integer }
              color: { type: string }
```

### Key fields
| Field | Meaning | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `metadata.name` | CRD object name | **must** be `<plural>.<group>` |
| `spec.group` | API group of the new kind | DNS-style, e.g. `stable.example.com` |
| `spec.scope` | `Namespaced` or `Cluster` | **immutable** after creation |
| `names.kind` | CR's `kind` value | PascalCase |
| `names.plural` | lowercase plural | used in REST path + `kubectl get` |
| `names.shortNames` | nicknames | optional |
| `versions[].served` | expose over REST | at least one must be `true` to use it |
| `versions[].storage` | persisted version | **exactly one** `true` |
| `schema.openAPIV3Schema` | structural schema | **required** in `v1`; must start `type: object` |

### Commands
```bash
kubectl apply -f widget-crd.yaml
kubectl get crd widgets.stable.example.com
# wait for it to be usable:
kubectl wait --for=condition=Established crd/widgets.stable.example.com --timeout=30s
# confirm the Established condition:
kubectl get crd widgets.stable.example.com \
  -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions[?(@.type=="Established")].status}'
# see the new kind register in discovery:
kubectl api-resources --api-group=stable.example.com
```

### Structural schema requirements (v1)
`apiextensions.k8s.io/v1` requires a **structural** `openAPIV3Schema`:
- top level must be `type: object`;
- every field has a `type` (or `x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: true`);
- no `type` at the root → the CRD is rejected.

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **`metadata.name` ≠ `<plural>.<group>`** → rejected immediately. The single most common mistake.
- **Confusing the two apiVersions**: the CRD is `apiextensions.k8s.io/v1`; the *CR* you create later uses `<group>/<version>` (`stable.example.com/v1`).
- **Missing top-level `type: object`** in the schema → CRD invalid.
- **No version served** → the kind is registered but you cannot create CRs (`server could not find the requested resource`).
- **More than one `storage: true`** (or zero) → rejected.
- **Established takes a moment** — apply then `kubectl wait --for=condition=Established` before creating CRs, or the CR apply may race and fail.
- `scope` is **immutable**; to change it you must delete and recreate the CRD.

### Quick reference
```bash
kubectl apply -f crd.yaml
kubectl wait --for=condition=Established crd/widgets.stable.example.com --timeout=30s
kubectl get crd                      # list all CRDs
kubectl explain widget.spec          # schema-driven docs for your new kind
```

questions.title: Create a custom resource
questions.teach:
Once a CRD is Established you create its custom resources like any native object with `kubectl apply`. The CR's `kind` is the CRD's `names.kind` (`Widget`) and its `spec` must match the schema. A Namespaced CRD's CRs live in a namespace.

**Gotcha:** the CR's `apiVersion` is `<group>/<version>` (`stable.example.com/v1`), NOT `apiextensions.k8s.io/v1` — that belongs to the CRD, not the CR.
questions.prompt:
In namespace `crd-learn`, create a `Widget` named `gadget` with `spec.size: 3` and `spec.color: blue`.

Target: `kubectl -n crd-learn get widget gadget` exists with `.spec.size == 3` and `.spec.color == blue`.
questions.hint: `apiVersion: stable.example.com/v1`, `kind: Widget`, `metadata.name: gadget`, `spec.size: 3`, `spec.color: blue`. Apply into `-n crd-learn`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl -n crd-learn apply -f -
apiVersion: stable.example.com/v1
kind: Widget
metadata:
  name: gadget
spec:
  size: 3
  color: blue
YAML
kubectl -n crd-learn get widget gadget -o jsonpath='{.spec.size}/{.spec.color}'

verification.description: Widget 'gadget' in crd-learn with size=3 color=blue

questions.eli5:
Last step you taught the warehouse clerk a new kind called **Widget** by handing over an instruction card (the CRD). Now you actually want to put a real Widget on a shelf.

Making a custom resource (a **CR**) is just filling out the order form for that kind. Think of it like ordering off a menu the chef just added: the dish exists now, so you write a normal order ticket:

- `kind: Widget` — the dish name from the menu,
- `apiVersion: stable.example.com/v1` — which menu and which edition it came from,
- a name for *this* Widget (`gadget`),
- a `spec` with the toppings the menu allows: `size: 3`, `color: blue`.

Then `kubectl apply` hands the ticket in, and the clerk files your Widget just like it files Pods or Services. You can `kubectl get widget gadget` to see it on the shelf.

Because Widget is **namespaced**, every Widget lives inside one room (`crd-learn`). You have to say which room when you create it and when you look for it.

**Watch out:**

- The CR's `apiVersion` is **`<group>/<version>`** (`stable.example.com/v1`) — **not** `apiextensions.k8s.io/v1`. That second one belongs to the *card*, not the Widget.
- The `kind` must be the **exact** `names.kind` from the CRD: `Widget`, capital W.
- The `spec` must fit the shape the card described (a number `size`, a text `color`), or the clerk rejects it.
- It's **namespaced**, so remember `-n crd-learn` both to create and to find it — look in the wrong room and it seems to vanish.
questions.deepDive:
## Creating a custom resource (CR) — full rundown

### Mental model
Once a CRD is **Established**, its `kind` behaves like any built-in kind. A **custom resource** is just an instance of that kind — you `apply` it, `get` it, `edit` it, `delete` it, and label it exactly as you would a Pod. The CRD defined the *class*; the CR is the *object*.

### The exact manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: stable.example.com/v1      # <group>/<version> — NOT apiextensions.k8s.io
kind: Widget                           # == CRD's spec.names.kind
metadata:
  name: gadget
  namespace: crd-learn                 # namespaced CRD → CR lives in a namespace
spec:
  size: 3                              # integer, per the schema
  color: blue                          # string, per the schema
```

```bash
kubectl -n crd-learn apply -f gadget.yaml
kubectl -n crd-learn get widget gadget
kubectl -n crd-learn get widget gadget -o jsonpath='{.spec.size}/{.spec.color}'
```

### Where each apiVersion comes from
| Object | `apiVersion` | `kind` |
|---|---|---|
| The CRD | `apiextensions.k8s.io/v1` | `CustomResourceDefinition` |
| The CR (Widget) | `stable.example.com/v1` | `Widget` |

Read the CR's `apiVersion` off the CRD: `group` + `/` + the version whose `served: true`.

### Inspecting CRs like native objects
```bash
kubectl -n crd-learn get widgets                 # list (plural)
kubectl -n crd-learn get widget gadget -o yaml   # full object
kubectl -n crd-learn describe widget gadget
kubectl -n crd-learn edit widget gadget          # in-place edit
kubectl explain widget.spec                       # schema-driven field docs
```

### Validation on apply
The apiserver validates the CR against the CRD's `openAPIV3Schema` at apply time:
- wrong type (`size: "big"` when schema says integer) → rejected;
- unknown field + structural schema → **pruned** (silently dropped), unless `x-kubernetes-preserve-unknown-fields: true`.

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **Wrong `apiVersion`** is the #1 error: using `apiextensions.k8s.io/v1` on the CR gives `no matches for kind "Widget"`.
- **Case-sensitive `kind`**: must match `names.kind` exactly (`Widget`, not `widget`).
- **Forgetting `-n`** on a namespaced CR: it's created in `default` or looked for in the wrong namespace and appears "missing."
- **Type mismatch** against the schema is rejected — quote strings, leave integers unquoted.
- The CRD must be **Established first**; applying a CR too early races and fails with `could not find the requested resource`.

### Quick reference
```bash
kubectl -n crd-learn apply -f gadget.yaml
kubectl -n crd-learn get widget gadget -o jsonpath='{.spec.size}/{.spec.color}'
# imperative-ish one-liner via stdin:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl -n crd-learn apply -f -
apiVersion: stable.example.com/v1
kind: Widget
metadata: { name: gadget }
spec: { size: 3, color: blue }
YAML
```

questions.title: List CRs by plural and short name
questions.teach:
A CRD registers a real kind, so its CRs list with the same verbs as native objects: `kubectl -n crd-learn get widgets` (plural), `get widget` (singular), and `get wg` (short name) all return the same objects.

**Gotcha:** for a Namespaced CRD, omitting `-n` lists only the current namespace — resources can look "empty" when they really exist elsewhere.
questions.prompt:
Create a **second** Widget named `widget2` in `crd-learn` (`spec.size: 7`, `spec.color: red`), so `kubectl -n crd-learn get widgets` shows two Widgets.

Target: namespace `crd-learn` contains at least two Widgets, including `widget2` (size=7, color=red).
questions.hint: Same shape as step 2 but `metadata.name: widget2`, `size: 7`, `color: red`. Verify with `kubectl -n crd-learn get wg` (the short name).
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl -n crd-learn apply -f -
apiVersion: stable.example.com/v1
kind: Widget
metadata:
  name: widget2
spec:
  size: 7
  color: red
YAML
kubectl -n crd-learn get wg

verification.description: crd-learn has >=2 Widgets including widget2 (size=7 color=red)

questions.eli5:
You've got one Widget on the shelf. Now you add a second so you can practice *finding* them.

Here's the nice part: because a CRD teaches Kubernetes a **real** kind, your Widgets answer to the same "roll call" as built-in things. It's like a librarian who will fetch a book whether you ask for its full title, its one-word nickname, or its catalog code — same book either way. For Widgets:

- `kubectl get widgets` — the **plural** (how you list a bunch),
- `kubectl get widget` — the **singular**,
- `kubectl get wg` — the **short name** (the nickname you put in `shortNames` on the card).

All three return the *same* Widgets. So after you create `widget2` (size 7, red) next to `gadget`, any of those commands shows **two** Widgets in the room.

**Watch out:**

- Widgets are **namespaced**, so `kubectl get widgets` only shows the **current room** (namespace). If you forget `-n crd-learn`, the list can look empty even though your Widgets are sitting right there in another room.
- The **short name `wg` only works if the CRD declared it** under `names.shortNames`. No declaration, no nickname.
- To peek across every room at once, use `-A` (all namespaces): `kubectl get widgets -A`.
- Plural/singular/short all point at the **same** kind — they're just different ways to say "Widget," not different objects.
questions.deepDive:
## Listing CRs by plural, singular, and short name — full rundown

### Mental model
A CRD registers its kind into the apiserver's **discovery** system, so `kubectl` treats it exactly like a native resource. The `names` block in the CRD declares all the aliases `kubectl` will accept: `kind`, `plural`, `singular`, and optional `shortNames`. Any alias resolves to the same REST endpoint and returns the same objects.

### Create a second CR
```yaml
apiVersion: stable.example.com/v1
kind: Widget
metadata:
  name: widget2
  namespace: crd-learn
spec:
  size: 7
  color: red
```
```bash
kubectl -n crd-learn apply -f widget2.yaml
```

### All the ways to list the same objects
| Command | Uses | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| `kubectl -n crd-learn get widgets` | plural | current namespace |
| `kubectl -n crd-learn get widget` | singular | current namespace |
| `kubectl -n crd-learn get wg` | shortName | current namespace |
| `kubectl get widgets -A` | plural | **all** namespaces |
| `kubectl get widgets.stable.example.com` | fully-qualified | disambiguates clashes |

```bash
kubectl -n crd-learn get widgets          # should show gadget AND widget2
kubectl -n crd-learn get wg -o wide
```

### Namespaced vs cluster scope in listing
- **Namespaced** CRD → `get` shows only the current namespace; use `-n <ns>` or `-A`.
- **Cluster** CRD → no namespace; `-A` is meaningless, just `kubectl get <plural>`.

### shortNames
`shortNames` live under `spec.names.shortNames: [wg]`. Only declared short names work; `kubectl get wg` fails if the CRD never listed `wg`. Check available names and short names:
```bash
kubectl api-resources --api-group=stable.example.com
# NAME      SHORTNAMES   APIVERSION                 NAMESPACED   KIND
# widgets   wg           stable.example.com/v1      true         Widget
```

### Disambiguating name clashes
If two groups both define a `widgets` plural, `kubectl get widgets` is ambiguous. Use the **fully qualified** form `get widgets.stable.example.com` to pin the group.

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **Forgetting `-n`** on a namespaced kind → list looks empty though CRs exist elsewhere. Reach for `-A` when unsure where something lives.
- **Short name only works if declared** in `names.shortNames`.
- `-A` is for namespaced kinds; for cluster-scoped kinds it does nothing useful.
- Plural / singular / short all hit the **same** endpoint — they are aliases, not distinct resources.
- Field selectors are limited on CRs; filter with labels (`-l`) or `-o jsonpath` instead.

### Quick reference
```bash
kubectl -n crd-learn get widgets            # plural
kubectl -n crd-learn get widget widget2     # singular + name
kubectl -n crd-learn get wg                  # short name
kubectl get widgets -A                       # across namespaces
kubectl api-resources --api-group=stable.example.com   # discover names/shortNames
```

questions.title: Cluster-scoped CRD
questions.teach:
`spec.scope` is either `Namespaced` or `Cluster`. A **Cluster**-scoped CRD's CRs live outside any namespace — you create and get them without `-n`, and `metadata.namespace` is ignored.

**Gotcha:** scope is fixed at creation; you cannot flip a CRD from Namespaced to Cluster later. `kubectl get <plural> -A` won't help for cluster-scoped kinds — just `kubectl get <plural>`.
questions.prompt:
Create a **Cluster**-scoped CRD for kind `Region` in group `stable.example.com` (plural `regions`, singular `region`, version `v1` served+storage, schema types `spec.zone` as string). Then create a cluster-scoped `Region` named `us-east` with `spec.zone: iad`.

Target: CRD `regions.stable.example.com` has scope `Cluster` and is Established; `kubectl get region us-east` exists with `.spec.zone == iad`.
questions.hint: In the CRD set `spec.scope: Cluster`. `metadata.name` = `regions.stable.example.com`. Create the `Region` CR with NO namespace: `kubectl get region us-east` (no `-n`).
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: regions.stable.example.com
spec:
  group: stable.example.com
  scope: Cluster
  names:
    kind: Region
    plural: regions
    singular: region
  versions:
  - name: v1
    served: true
    storage: true
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          spec:
            type: object
            properties:
              zone: { type: string }
YAML
kubectl wait --for=condition=Established crd/regions.stable.example.com --timeout=30s
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: stable.example.com/v1
kind: Region
metadata:
  name: us-east
spec:
  zone: iad
YAML
kubectl get region us-east -o jsonpath='{.spec.zone}'

verification.description: CRD regions.stable.example.com scope=Cluster Established; Region us-east with zone=iad

questions.eli5:
So far your Widgets lived **inside rooms** (namespaces). Some things, though, don't belong to any one room — they belong to the whole building. Think of **fire extinguishers** or the building's **Wi-Fi network**: there's no "room" that owns them; they just exist building-wide.

A **Cluster-scoped** CRD is for exactly that kind of thing. When you set `spec.scope: Cluster` on the card, every custom resource of that kind lives **out in the open**, not in any namespace. You create a `Region` without picking a room, and you look it up without a room either:

- `kubectl get region us-east` — no `-n` anywhere.

Everything else is the same as before: pick a group, give it names, serve a version, describe the shape (`spec.zone` is text). Only the **scope** changes.

**Watch out:**

- **Scope is set once and frozen.** You can't later flip a CRD from Namespaced to Cluster (or back). Pick correctly at creation, or delete and recreate.
- For cluster-scoped kinds, **don't use `-n` and don't use `-A`** — there are no namespaces to list across. Just `kubectl get regions`.
- If you put `metadata.namespace` on a cluster-scoped CR, it's **ignored** — the object isn't really in that room.
- Still wait for **`Established: True`** before creating the CR, same as any CRD.
- The CR's `apiVersion` is still `<group>/<version>` (`stable.example.com/v1`) — the Cluster scope doesn't change that.
questions.deepDive:
## Cluster-scoped CRDs — full rundown

### Mental model
`spec.scope` decides whether a CRD's resources belong to a namespace or to the whole cluster. **Namespaced** kinds (Pods, Deployments, your earlier Widget) live inside one namespace. **Cluster**-scoped kinds (Nodes, PersistentVolumes, StorageClasses) exist once across the whole cluster with no namespace. You set this when authoring the CRD — it is **immutable** afterward.

### The exact manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: regions.stable.example.com      # <plural>.<group>
spec:
  group: stable.example.com
  scope: Cluster                         # <- the difference
  names:
    kind: Region
    plural: regions
    singular: region
  versions:
  - name: v1
    served: true
    storage: true
    schema:
      openAPIV3Schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          spec:
            type: object
            properties:
              zone: { type: string }
```
The cluster-scoped CR (no namespace):
```yaml
apiVersion: stable.example.com/v1
kind: Region
metadata:
  name: us-east                          # NO namespace field needed/used
spec:
  zone: iad
```
```bash
kubectl apply -f region-crd.yaml
kubectl wait --for=condition=Established crd/regions.stable.example.com --timeout=30s
kubectl apply -f us-east.yaml
kubectl get region us-east -o jsonpath='{.spec.zone}'
```

### Namespaced vs Cluster
| Aspect | `Namespaced` | `Cluster` |
|---|---|---|
| CR lives in | a namespace | no namespace (cluster-wide) |
| Create with | `-n <ns>` | no `-n` |
| List with | `-n <ns>` or `-A` | plain `kubectl get <plural>` |
| `metadata.namespace` | required/used | **ignored** |
| Changeable later | no | no (**immutable**) |
| Native examples | Pod, Deployment | Node, PV, StorageClass, ClusterRole |

### Commands
```bash
kubectl get regions                      # list cluster-scoped CRs
kubectl get crd regions.stable.example.com \
  -o jsonpath='{.spec.scope}'            # => Cluster
kubectl get region us-east -o yaml
```

### Gotchas & exam traps
- **Scope is immutable.** You cannot patch a CRD from `Namespaced` to `Cluster`; delete and recreate (which also deletes its CRs).
- **No `-n`, no `-A`** for cluster-scoped kinds. `kubectl get regions -A` is meaningless; `-n foo` is ignored.
- A `metadata.namespace` on a cluster-scoped CR is silently **ignored** — don't assume it placed the object anywhere.
- Still requires a **structural schema** (`type: object` root) and **exactly one** `storage: true` version, same as any v1 CRD.
- Wait for **Established** before creating CRs, or you race the registration.
- The CR's `apiVersion` is still `<group>/<version>` — scope doesn't change that.

### Quick reference
```bash
# CRD: set scope Cluster
kubectl get crd regions.stable.example.com -o jsonpath='{.spec.scope}'   # Cluster
kubectl wait --for=condition=Established crd/regions.stable.example.com --timeout=30s
# CR: no namespace
kubectl get region us-east -o jsonpath='{.spec.zone}'                     # iad
```
